candidate_findings.title: Mutation and recovery commands lack atomic authorization and replay semantics
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt names hard-gated approval, graph-patch, remote-side-effect, and safe-point recovery actions but does not bind them to compare-and-set preconditions, idempotency, authorization rechecks, or partial-failure behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A delayed, duplicated, or replayed command can approve an obsolete blocked episode, patch the wrong graph generation, or restore/retry against a worktree whose head changed, risking unauthorized side effects or lost work.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Require server-side authorization at execution; run/node/attempt/blocked_sequence/generation/worktree-head preconditions; idempotency keys and replay results; confirmation policy; timeout and cancellation semantics; transactional or compensating behavior for restore-then-retry; and durable audit receipts.

candidate_findings.title: Projection trust cannot deterministically gate live claims or actions
candidate_findings.claim: The core requires stale/degraded disclosure and sometimes gating, but uses discretionary phrases such as 'likely', 'may survive', and 'may gate' without defining trust states, thresholds, authority, or recovery.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two surfaces can show incompatible live truth or enable different actions from the same stale projection, and users cannot tell whether an action is safe after a disconnect or delayed update.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the trust-state enum, authoritative source and version/epoch, staleness calculation and clock rules, per-state rendering and action matrix, monotonic update ordering, reconnect/resync behavior, stale-command rejection, and deterministic recovery criteria.
